issues.description: Regex `/\dm?s/i` matches substrings like 'ms' inside identifiers or URLs, causing false positives that still hit the slow path.
issues.detail: The fast-reject is fine — false positives only cost what the old code already paid. But e.g. `background: url(thumbs.png)` contains 's' adjacent to a digit context in some values, and identifiers like `1s-foo` or `dimensions` could match. It's a perf hint, not a correctness gate, so it's acceptable. Worth a one-line comment noting it's intentionally loose.

issues.description: No test demonstrating the perf win or guarding against regex regression.
issues.detail: Patch claims a perf fix but ships zero benchmark or test. For a one-line regex fast-path in a linter rule that runs on every decl, a fixture confirming the rule still flags everything it used to (and skips what it should skip) is the bare minimum. Existing tests presumably cover behavior; confirm they pass and call it done.

review.summary: Small, scoped, readable patch. Moves the cheap reject before the expensive `valueParser` call and skips the `vendor.unprefixed`/`toLowerCase` work when the value obviously has no time token. This is exactly the shape a perf patch should take: one diff, one purpose, no gratuitous abstraction. GOOD-TASTE: the early-return eliminates the special case of "parse everything then discover it was nothing." Verdict: ACCEPT. Regex is intentionally loose as a fast-path filter — that's fine, the slow path still validates correctly.
